new_today.title: Integration of polygenic risk with single cell methylation data using met-scDRS.
new_today.title_zh: 使用met-scDRS将多基因风险与单细胞甲基化数据整合。
new_today.summary_zh: 尽管大规模全基因组关联研究（GWAS）已识别出许多精神疾病性状的风险变异，但其功能含义仍 largely 未知。其风险的潜在机制之一是通过细胞背景依赖性表观遗传学如甲基化。先前方法侧重于将GWAS与单细胞转录组学整合，从而能够识别疾病风险关联的细胞类型内异质性。我们将此框架扩展为一种名为met-scDRS的方法，将GWAS与单细胞表观基因组学整合，并研究精神疾病风险如何通过单细胞分辨率的甲基化组学体现。我们提出一种方法，将单细胞甲基化组与GWAS识别的疾病相关基因在单细胞分辨率下整合。我们发现我们的方法在不同场景下校准良好且具有功效。然后我们分析了公开可用的人脑单细胞甲基化组数据集中的75种不同性状，并为每种性状的每个细胞生成疾病相关性评分。我们发现高脑特异性，主要细胞类型富集与已知发现一致。我们识别了沿大脑空间轴的精神疾病风险的细胞类型内异质性以及与疾病差异相关的亚群。最后，我们表明甲基

extra.description: Although large scale genome-wide association studies (GWAS) have identified many risk variants for psychiatric traits their functional implication remain largely unknown. One potential mechanism for their risk is through cellular context-dependent epigenetics such as methylation. Previous methodologies have focused on integrating GWAS with single cell transcriptomics, which allowed identification of within-cell-type heterogeneity in disease risk association. We extended this framework to provide a method called met-scDRS that integrates GWAS with single cell epigenomics and investigates how psychiatric disease risk can manifest through methylomics at single cell resolution. We propose an approach that integrates single cell methylomes with disease associated genes identified from GWAS at single-cell resolution. We found our method to be well calibrated and powered in different scenarios. We then analyzed a publicly available single cell methylome dataset of the human brain for 75 different traits and generated disease relevance scores for each cell for each trait. We find high brain specificity with major cell type enrichments congruent with known findings. We identify within-cell-type heterogeneity for psychiatric disease risk along the brain spatial axis as well as subpopulations that are differentially associated with diseases. Finally, we showed that genes with high correlation between methylation levels and disease relevance scores to be highly enriched in specific functional pathways such as synaptic formation and transmission. met-scDRS is freely available in GitHub as a python package under MIT license: https://github.com/bogdanlab/met-scDRS. Source code is also available from Zenodo with DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.21841506. All dataset used in this work are publicly available. Supplementary data are available at Bioinformatics online.

new_today.title: HRD: an integrated multi-omics resource for human reproduction and development
new_today.title_zh: HRD：人类生殖与发育的综合多组学资源
new_today.summary_zh: 摘要 人类生殖与发育是一个由遗传、分子和环境因素塑造的连续过程。然而，相关数据仍分散在公共存储库和文献中，限制了系统整合、分析和再利用。我们开发了人类生殖与发育数据库（HRD；http://www.inbirg.com/hrd/），这是一个综合多组学资源，组织与多个生殖、妊娠和发育背景相关的公开可用数据。HRD 1.0版包含814条组学记录，包括432条批量转录组、144条单细胞或单核转录组、156条表观基因组、52条代谢组和30条蛋白质组记录，以及702条临床试验记录、293条暴露-结局关联和779个带有 curated 表型关联的先导SNP。通过协调关键元数据并应用数据类型特定的分析工作流，HRD将组学数据、遗传关联、暴露-结局证据和临床试验数据纳入一个共同框架，以探索生殖和发育多个阶段的数据。该网站支持关键词搜索、组合筛选、基于类别的浏览、统计摘要和数据下载，并提供差异分析、功能富集

extra.description: Abstract Human reproduction and development span a continuum shaped by genetic, molecular, and environmental factors. However, relevant data remain dispersed across public repositories and the literature, limiting systematic integration, analysis, and reuse. We developed the Human Reproduction and Development Database (HRD; http://www.inbirg.com/hrd/), an integrated multi-omics resource that organizes publicly available data relevant to multiple reproductive, pregnancy, and developmental contexts. HRD version 1.0 contains 814 omics records, including 432 bulk transcriptomic, 144 single-cell or single-nucleus transcriptomic, 156 epigenomic, 52 metabolomic, and 30 proteomic records, together with 702 clinical trial records, 293 exposure-outcome associations, and 779 lead SNPs with curated phenotype associations. By harmonising key metadata and applying data-type-specific analysis workflows, HRD brings omics data, genetic associations, exposure-outcome evidence, and clinical trial data into a common framework for exploring data from multiple stages of reproduction and development. The website supports keyword search, combined filtering, category-based browsing, statistical summaries and data downloads, and provides interactive visualizations of differential analyses, functional enrichment, cell clustering, chromatin accessibility, peak annotation, regulatory networks, and cross-phenotype association plots. HRD supports the retrieval, comparison, and reuse of reproductive and developmental data and analysis results.

dropped.summary_zh: 人类生殖与发育是一个由遗传、分子和环境因素塑造的连续过程。然而，相关数据仍分散在公共存储库和文献中，限制了系统性整合、分析和复用。我们开发了人类生殖与发育数据库（HRD；http://www.inbirg.com/hrd/），这是一个整合多组学资源，用于组织与多种生殖、妊娠和发育情境相关的公开可用数据。HRD 1.0版包含814条组学记录，包括432条bulk转录组、144条单细胞或单核转录组、156条表观基因组、52条代谢组和30条蛋白质组记录，以及702条临床试验记录、293条暴露-结局关联和779个带有 curated 表型关联的 lead SNP。通过协调关键元数据并应用数据类型特定的分析流程，HRD将组学数据、遗传关联、暴露-结局证据和临床试验数据纳入一个共同框架，用于探索生殖与发育多个阶段的数据。该网站支持关键词搜索、组合筛选、基于类别的浏览、统计摘要和数据下载，并提供差异分析

extra.description: Human reproduction and development span a continuum shaped by genetic, molecular, and environmental factors. However, relevant data remain dispersed across public repositories and the literature, limiting systematic integration, analysis, and reuse. We developed the Human Reproduction and Development Database (HRD; http://www.inbirg.com/hrd/), an integrated multi-omics resource that organizes publicly available data relevant to multiple reproductive, pregnancy, and developmental contexts. HRD version 1.0 contains 814 omics records, including 432 bulk transcriptomic, 144 single-cell or single-nucleus transcriptomic, 156 epigenomic, 52 metabolomic, and 30 proteomic records, together with 702 clinical trial records, 293 exposure-outcome associations, and 779 lead SNPs with curated phenotype associations. By harmonising key metadata and applying data-type-specific analysis workflows, HRD brings omics data, genetic associations, exposure-outcome evidence, and clinical trial data into a common framework for exploring data from multiple stages of reproduction and development. The website supports keyword search, combined filtering, category-based browsing, statistical summaries and data downloads, and provides interactive visualizations of differential analyses, functional enrichment, cell clustering, chromatin accessibility, peak annotation, regulatory networks, and cross-phenotype association plots. HRD supports the retrieval, comparison, and reuse of reproductive and developmental data and analysis results.

dropped.title: Miro1 mediates skeletal muscle insulin resistance in type 2 diabetes.
dropped.title_zh: Miro1 介导 2 型糖尿病中的骨骼肌胰岛素抵抗。
dropped.summary_zh: 骨骼肌线粒体动力学失衡通过尚不完全清楚的机制促成 2 型糖尿病（T2D）的发生和进展。在此，我们研究了线粒体 Rho GTPase 1（Miro1），一种线粒体外膜酶，在 2 型糖尿病（T2D）中调控骨骼肌胰岛素作用和葡萄糖稳态的作用。在一项横断面临床研究中，我们显示 Miro1 在肥胖和 T2D 患者的骨骼肌中积累，这一现象在 T2D 小鼠模型中进一步得到重现。这种积累可由线粒体外膜上 AKT 与 Miro1 之间胰岛素介导的相互作用不足来解释。在一项随机对照试验（NCT02977442）中，我们显示运动训练可缓解 T2D 患者骨骼肌 Miro1 积累，同时改善胰岛素敏感性。肌肉特异性 Miro1 缺失可改善小鼠和细胞的氧化能力和胰岛素敏感性。综上，这些数据支持骨骼肌 Miro1 在 T2D 病理生理中的关键调控作用。ClinicalTrials.gov 标识符：NCT02977442。

extra.description: Imbalanced skeletal muscle mitochondrial dynamics contribute to the onset and progression of type 2 diabetes (T2D) by mechanisms that remain incompletely understood. Here, we examined the role of Mitochondrial Rho GTPase 1 (Miro1), an outer mitochondrial membrane enzyme, in regulating skeletal muscle insulin action and glucose homeostasis in type 2 diabetes (T2D). In a cross-sectional clinical study, we show that Miro1 accumulates in the skeletal muscle of patients with obesity and T2D, which was further replicated in mouse models of T2D. This accumulation is explained by inadequate insulin-mediated interaction between AKT and Miro1 at the outer mitochondrial membrane. In a randomized controlled trial (NCT02977442), we show that exercise training relieves skeletal muscle Miro1 accumulation while improving insulin sensitivity in patients with T2D. Muscle-specific Miro1 deletion improves oxidative capacity and insulin sensitivity in mice and cells. Taken together, these data support a key regulatory role for skeletal muscle Miro1 in the pathophysiology of T2D. ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT02977442.

longest_on_board.summary_zh: 单细胞RNA测序（scRNA-seq）下游分析的一个核心挑战是高维小样本（HDSS）情形，且常因稀有细胞类型而加剧类别不平衡。这些因素阻碍了稳健的特征（基因）选择和细胞聚类，并限制了现有模拟器生成样本的真实性。我们提出GARAGE，一种图注意力稀有细胞感知单细胞数据生成方法，在先验噪声之外，用少量、注意力加权的真实细胞“泄漏”来增强生成器输入。具体来说，我们构建k近邻细胞图，并使用图注意力网络（GAT）优先选择可能代表欠采样（稀有）亚群的节点；这些高注意力细胞嵌入被注入生成器输入，以引导合成朝向数据流形中生物学上合理的区域，同时尊重细胞类型比例。这种注意力引导泄漏加速训练，减少模式丢失，并生成保留稀有细胞结构的真实合成细胞。在真实scRNA-seq基准上，GARAGE相比最先进基线改善了下游特征选择和聚类。总之，GARAGE通过将图注意力与对抗生成结合，直接应对scRNA-seq中的HDS

extra.description: A central challenge in downstream single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) analysis is the high-dimensional, small-sample (HDSS) regime, often compounded by class imbalance from rare cell types. These factors hinder robust feature (gene) selection and cell clustering and limit the realism of samples generated by existing simulators. We introduce GARAGE , a G raph- A ttentive RA re-cell aware single-cell data GE neration that augments the generator’s input with a small, attention-weighted ‘leakage’ of real cells in addition to prior noise. extra.description: Abstract Cancer subtype classification based on molecular features is important for characterizing tumor heterogeneity, evaluating patient prognosis, and supporting precision treatment. Multi-omics integration provides complementary molecular information across genomic, epigenomic, transcriptomic, and proteomic levels. However, the high dimensionality of multi-omics data, complex cross-omics relationships, and imbalanced subtype distributions remain major challenges. To address these issues, we propose CALT-GNN, a graph neural network framework that integrates patient-similarity graph learning, cross-attention-based omics integration, long-tail expert classification, and learnable prediction fusion. The framework first constructs omics-specific patient-similarity graphs, learns latent patient representations using graph convolutional networks, and obtains a unified graph through similarity network fusion. A cross-attention branch models complementary relationships between CNA and DNA methylation as source modalities and mRNA expression as the target modality. In parallel, a long-tail expert branch uses Major and Minor Experts with prototype-guided routing to perform class-distribution-aware classification. The outputs of the two branches are subsequently combined using a learnable global weight. Experiments on eight TCGA multi-omics cohorts showed that CALT-GNN achieved competitive or comparable classification performance relative to representative baseline methods and stable performance on Macro-F1 and MCC, which are sensitive to class imbalance. Ablation and subtype-level analyses further supported the complementary contributions of cross-omics interaction modeling and adaptive long-tail expert routing, although the magnitude of the improvements varied across cohorts and subtypes. These results suggest that CALT-GNN provides a methodological framework for multi-omics cancer subtype classification under complex cross-omics relationships and imbalanced subtype distributions.

extra.description: Imaging-based spatially resolved transcriptomics (imSRT) technologies provide high-throughput molecular-resolution spatial characterization of genes within cells. Conventional analysis methods to identify cell-types and states in imSRT data rely on gene count matrices derived from tallying the number of mRNA molecules detected for each gene per segmented cell, thereby overlooking subcellular heterogeneity that can be useful in defining cell states. To take advantage of the molecular-resolution information in imSRT data and potentially identify cell-states based on subcellular heterogeneity, we developed STARIT (Spatial Transcriptomics As Rasterized Image Tensors). STARIT converts transcripts within segmented cells in imSRT data into an image-based tensor representation that can be combined with deep learning computer vision models for downstream analysis. Using simulated and real imSRT data, we demonstrate that STARIT distinguishes transcriptionally distinct cell-types and further separates cell states based on subcellular transcript localization, which conventional gene count analysis fails to capture. By providing a standardized framework to encode subcellular molecular information in imSRT data, STARIT will enable deeper insights into subcellular heterogeneity and enhance the identification and characterization of cell-types and states that are overlooked by gene count representations.

longest_on_board.summary_zh: 随着云计算与空天地海一体化通信网络的深度融合, 各种复杂应用场景的出现使得组合服务的种类和数量急剧增多, 结构也变得复杂。在云网融合环境下, 用户移动设备和边缘服务器等硬件能力有限, 能耗问题成为组合服务进行动态重构不可忽略的重要因素。此外, 传统方法并未考虑空天地海不同场景下用户对不同服务质量(QoS)属性需求的差异性, 使得组合服务的交付结果并不令人满意。为了解决上述问题, 提出一种基于多目标粒子群优化(PSO)的组合服务动态重构方法。该方法首先根据重构原子服务的三维空间地理位置和功能进行聚类, 有效解决在云网融合环境下服务规模庞大情况下的搜索空间爆炸问题; 然后通过能耗计算模型得到服务调用的综合能耗, 并将其作为动态重构的优化目标之一, 结合服务的多种QoS属性进行多目标寻优, 最终生成符合用户需求且能耗较低的重构方案。实验结果表明, 该方法在云网融合环境下节约能耗和应对较大候选服务

longest_on_board.title: 基于多信息融合的高速收费站拥堵检测算法
longest_on_board.title_zh: 基于多信息融合的高速收费站拥堵检测算法
longest_on_board.summary_zh: 在高速收费站拥堵检测场景中, 遮挡、阴影、景深等因素严重影响检测算法的精度, 基于单信息的拥堵检测算法无法准确反映收费站真实拥堵情况, 对此, 提出一种高速收费站多信息融合拥堵检测算法。首先采用目标检测算法检测目标区域车辆, 利用图像空间特征计算车道占用率; 其次利用Deep SORT目标跟踪算法与滑动平衡机制进行车流量综合估计, 减少因为遮挡和阴影导致的车辆误检、漏检问题; 最后利用基于光流信息熵的车速估计方法, 降低因景深变化导致的拥堵状态检测误差。通过融合3种不同维度信息得到拥堵指数, 拥堵指数聚类为5种拥堵类别以判断真实拥堵状态, 从而实现高速收费站的拥堵检测。实验结果表明, 在高速收费站拥堵数据集上, 采用多信息融合的拥堵检测算法准确率达到90.4%, 能够实现对收费站拥堵状态的准确检测。
